title: Logistic Regression
description: Foundational linear classifier predicting category probabilities.
name: Logistic Regression
summary: Logistic Regression measures the relationship between the categorical dependent variable and one or more independent variables by estimating probabilities using a logistic/sigmoid function.
use_when: Performing binary classification where probability calibration and model interpretability are critical.
avoid_when: Decision boundaries are complex and non-linear, and deep tree ensembles are available.
pros: Outputs well-calibrated probabilities rather than just hard classifications.
Low computational overhead makes it suitable for massive dataset scales.
Easily regularized using L1 or L2 norms to prevent overfitting.
cons: Cannot solve non-linear classification problems without manual feature engineering.
Requires large sample sizes for stable parameter estimation.
Vulnerable to multicollinearity and irrelevant features.

key_hyperparams.name: C
key_hyperparams.note: Inverse of regularization strength; smaller values specify stronger regularization.

quick_start:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5]])
y = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
clf = LogisticRegression().fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict([[2.5, 3.5]])
